findings.text: With no chip on, "Needs you 18" sits above a pinned "Waiting on you 15" (shots/inbox-none-1920.png, top band). The two disagree. rail.css:570 hides the pins whenever a chip is on, on the grounds that "Needs you is the same set", so either make the two rules one rule (DashRow.card_waits / of_ask vs WaitingOnYou) or say why they differ.

New shows 313 rows (shots/inbox-new-400.png) because DashChips.js:359 counts every `idle` task as new, however old it is. Abandoned idle tasks will bloat "new work". Consider limiting idle tasks to recent ones, or show idle under its own chip.

An ask with status `parked` counts as waiting and needs:true (DashRow.js:455, 470), so it lands under Needs you. The brief said "asks marked needs-owner"; a parked ask is not obviously waiting on the owner.

`walk_dirty` (State.mjs:67) makes the second count incremental. It re-reads only the files fs.watch marked, and the fold re-reads the same dirty set. A missed watch event now hits both counts the same way until the 10-minute rewalk, which weakens the "different discovery" proof in Server/doc/state.md. The speed gain (2.4 s down to 0.65 s) is real; the trade-off should be written in state.md.
